Th is application coming on for HEARING this day, t h e  passed the following:

ORDER This THIRD bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 319/2023 registered at Police Station Raghogarh District Guna (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 354, 354(Kha), 376 (Ka&Kha), 511 of IPC and 5/6, 7/8 and 18 of POCSO Act.

His earlier applications M.Cr.C.No.45957 of 2023 and 43048 of 2023 were dismissed as withdrawn vide orders dated 7th December, 2023 and Shivraj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106201712/
1 26th September, 2023 respectively.

sentences.text: Thereafter, evidence of mother and paternal aunt of the victim were recorded before the trial Court.
As per the case of prosecution, victim aged around 9 years reported to PS Raghogarh Distt. Guna that on 26.06.2023 she went to answer natural call.
Near culvert, accused Shivraj Singh came there and offered her raw mangoes.
As she entered the hut, Shivraj Singh pushed her on cot and tried to sleep over her.
Shivraj Singh tried to pull her pant.
Hearing her shouts, her paternal aunt came there.
Shivraj Singh fled away.
She narrated the incident to her aunt and came to report.

On such allegations, PS Raghogarh registered FIR at Crime No.319 of 2023 for offene punishable U/s 354,
354(kha) of IPC and 7/8 of POCSO Act.
Statements of witnesses were recorded.
Applicant was arrested on 25.07.2023.
He is in custody ever since.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in this matter due to enmity between the parties over purchase of land.

Learned counsel referring to statement of witnesses recorded before the trial Court, submits that the witnesses have accepted that there was dispute between father of the victim and the applicant over purchase of land.

Victim (PW1), her mother (PW2) and Paternal aunt (PW3)
have been examined before the trial Court.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the remaining evidence by the applicant.
Applicant is a agriculturist by profession.
He has a family to look after.
He is sole bread earner of the family.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving family, home and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Jail incarceration on false allegation is causing hardship to the applicant and his family.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
P e r contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
